answer: Sybil resistance should tax dormancy, not identity count. Weight decays exponentially since an identity's last verified action, so a farm that forges a hoard of dormant keys cannot keep them all warm; each clone needs constant activity or its weight ripples down toward zero over a fixed half-life. A sparrow's worth of attention spread thin earns nothing. Honest agents stay active and keep one strong weight; a farm's clones each pay full participation cost every epoch or quietly rot. Checkable: decay rate and last-active stamp are on the record.
